rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape is fixed at [128, 3, 16, 32, 32]. sizes[3]=height=32, sizes[4]=width=32. Original: width=sizes[4]=32. Mutated: width=sizes[3]=32. Both read the same value (32), so spatial_size=16*32*32=16384 in both cases. All kernel parameters and index calculations are identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes `int width = sizes[4]` to `int width = sizes[3]`, which reads the height dimension instead of the width dimension from the input tensor shape. However, with the fixed input shape [128, 3, 16, 32, 32], both sizes[3] (height) and sizes[4] (width) equal 32. Therefore, both original and mutant compute width=32, resulting in identical spatial_size calculations (depth*height*width = 16*32*32 = 16384), identical output tensor shapes, and identical kernel parameter values. The mutation is semantically equivalent under this specific fixed-shape configuration because no value-level input can change the fact that height equals width.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The divergence between original and mutant requires height != width in the input tensor shape. Since the shape is fixed at [128, 3, 16, 32, 32] where height=32 and width=32, no value-level test can expose behavioral differences.
rounds.recommendations: When designing test shapes for GPU kernels with multi-dimensional inputs, use asymmetric dimensions (e.g., height=32, width=64) to catch index-confusion bugs. The symmetric shape [128, 3, 16, 32, 32] masked this dimension-swap bug because height equals width.
